pinyin: bìng cóng kǒu rù, huò cóng kǒu chū
literal: illness · from · mouth · enter, disaster · from · mouth · exit
natural: Illness enters by the mouth, trouble comes out of it

meaning.en: Sickness comes from what you eat, and trouble comes from what you say.
meaning.zh: 疾病多因饮食不洁而来，祸事常因说话不慎而起。

equivalents: Loose lips sink ships
Mind what you eat and what you say

examples.zh: 俗话说，病从口入，祸从口出，吃饭要讲卫生，说话更要小心。
examples.en: As the saying goes, illness enters through the mouth and trouble comes out of it, so be careful about hygiene and about what you say.

examples.zh: 奶奶常叮嘱我们：病从口入，祸从口出。
examples.en: Grandma often warned us: watch what goes in and what comes out of your mouth.

usage.en: Said as a warning, usually to children or to someone who talks too freely. Often quoted in full.
usage.zh: 多用于告诫，常整句引用。

text: 朝霞不出门，晚霞行千里
pinyin: zhāo xiá bù chū mén, wǎn xiá xíng qiān lǐ
variants: 早霞不出门，晚霞行千里
literal: morning · glow · not · go out · door, evening · glow · travel · thousand · li
natural: Morning glow, stay in; evening glow, travel far

meaning.en: A red sky in the morning means bad weather, while a red sky at night promises fine weather.
meaning.zh: 早晨出现朝霞，往往要变天下雨；傍晚出现晚霞，第二天多是晴天。

equivalents: Red sky at night, shepherd's delight; red sky in the morning, shepherd's warning

examples.zh: 朝霞不出门，晚霞行千里，今天一早满天红霞，还是别爬山了。
examples.en: Red sky in the morning, so stay in; we'd better not climb the mountain today.

examples.zh: 爷爷看着天边的晚霞说：朝霞不出门，晚霞行千里，明天准是好天气。
examples.en: Looking at the evening glow, Grandpa said tomorrow would surely be fine.

usage.en: A weather proverb from farming and travelling life; often quoted in full.
usage.zh: 农谚，用来预测天气，常整句引用。

pinyin: tiān xià méi yǒu bù sàn de yán xí
variants: 千里搭长棚，没有不散的宴席
literal: under heaven · there is no · not · disperse · 's · feast
natural: No feast in the world lasts forever

meaning.en: Every gathering must come to an end, so partings are inevitable.
meaning.zh: 再热闹的聚会也有结束的时候，人终究要分别。

equivalents: All good things must come to an end
Every party has to end

examples.zh: 天下没有不散的筵席，毕业以后大家各奔东西了。
examples.en: All good things come to an end; after graduation everyone went their separate ways.

examples.zh: 别难过了，天下没有不散的筵席，我们以后常联系。
examples.en: Don't be sad, every party ends; we'll keep in touch.

usage.en: Said at farewells, to console or to accept parting. Warm, slightly wistful.
usage.zh: 多用于离别时的宽慰或感叹。

pinyin: zhǐ lǐ bāo bú zhù huǒ
literal: paper · inside · wrap · not · live · fire
natural: You can't wrap fire in paper

meaning.en: The truth cannot be hidden forever; sooner or later it will come out.
meaning.zh: 事实真相无法掩盖，终究会暴露出来。

equivalents: Truth will out
Murder will out
You can't keep a secret forever

examples.zh: 他以为贪污的事没人知道，可纸里包不住火，最后还是被查出来了。
examples.en: He thought nobody knew about the embezzlement, but the truth always comes out, and he was eventually caught.

examples.zh: 纸里包不住火，你还是主动向老师坦白吧。
examples.en: The truth will come out anyway, so you'd better confess to the teacher yourself.

usage.en: Used of scandals, lies and wrongdoing. Usually a warning; the pinyin is bāo bù zhù (bú before a fourth tone).
usage.zh: 多指丑事、谎言终会败露，常作警告。

pinyin: shī bài shì chéng gōng zhī mǔ
literal: failure · is · success · 's · mother
natural: Failure is the mother of success

meaning.en: Setbacks teach us lessons that lead to eventual success.
meaning.zh: 失败能让人总结教训，从而走向成功。

equivalents: Failure is the mother of success
Fall down seven times, get up eight

examples.zh: 别灰心，失败是成功之母，再试一次吧。
examples.en: Don't lose heart; failure is the mother of success, so try once more.

examples.zh: 失败是成功之母，这次考砸了正好找找原因。
examples.en: Failure is the mother of success; this bad exam is a good chance to find out why.

usage.en: Encouragement after a setback. Very common in school and workplace pep talks.
usage.zh: 用于失败后的鼓励，十分常用。

pinyin: hǎo hàn bù chī yǎn qián kuī
literal: good · fellow · not · eat · before · eyes · loss
natural: A real man doesn't take a loss right in front of him

meaning.en: A smart person avoids a losing confrontation and yields for now rather than suffer immediately.
meaning.zh: 聪明人遇到不利局面，先暂时避让，免得当下吃亏。

equivalents: Discretion is the better part of valour
He who fights and runs away lives to fight another day

examples.zh: 对方人多，好汉不吃眼前亏，我们先走吧。
examples.en: They outnumber us, and discretion is the better part of valour, so let's go.

examples.zh: 好汉不吃眼前亏，这笔钱先付了，回头再找他们理论。
examples.en: No point taking a loss now; I'll pay first and argue with them later.

usage.en: Often used to justify backing down; casual, can be self-mocking.
usage.zh: 常用来为暂时退让找台阶，口语，有时带自嘲。

pinyin: dé ráo rén chù qiě ráo rén
literal: get · to forgive · person · place · then · forgive · person
natural: Where you can forgive, forgive

meaning.en: Be lenient with others whenever you can, and don't push people too hard.
meaning.zh: 能宽容别人的地方就宽容，不要得理不饶人。

equivalents: Forgive and forget
Show mercy where you can

examples.zh: 他已经道歉了，得饶人处且饶人，别再追究了。
examples.en: He has apologised already; be forgiving and let it go.

examples.zh: 做人要得饶人处且饶人，把人逼到绝路对谁都没好处。
examples.en: Be lenient when you can; driving someone into a corner helps nobody.

usage.en: Advice to be generous; usually paired with 且饶人 as a whole line (得理不饶人 is the opposite attitude).
usage.zh: 劝人宽容，常整句使用；与“得理不饶人”相反。

pinyin: wú shì bù dēng sān bǎo diàn
literal: no · matter · not · climb · three · treasure · hall
natural: No business, no visit to the Hall of the Three Treasures

meaning.en: I only come to see you when I need something.
meaning.zh: 没有事情是不会来找你的，来了就是有事相求。

equivalents: I wouldn't be here if I didn't want something

examples.zh: 无事不登三宝殿，我今天来是想请你帮个忙。
examples.en: I wouldn't be here for nothing; I've come to ask you a favour.

examples.zh: 你无事不登三宝殿，说吧，找我什么事？
examples.en: You never come without a reason; go on, what do you want?

usage.en: Often said by the visitor, half-apologetically, before asking a favour; or teasingly by the host. Three Treasures = Buddha, Dharma, Sangha.
usage.zh: 来访者求人时的客套话，或主人打趣之语。三宝指佛、法、僧。

pinyin: yǎn bú jiàn, xīn bù fán
literal: eye · not · see, heart · not · vexed
natural: If the eyes don't see it, the heart isn't bothered

meaning.en: If you don't see something unpleasant, it won't upset you.
meaning.zh: 看不到令人烦心的事，心里就不会烦恼。

equivalents: Out of sight, out of mind
What the eye doesn't see, the heart doesn't grieve over

examples.zh: 房间太乱了，不过眼不见，心不烦，我把门关上就行。
examples.en: The room is a mess, but out of sight, out of mind; I'll just shut the door.

examples.zh: 他把手机扔进抽屉，想着眼不见，心不烦。
examples.en: He tossed his phone in a drawer, thinking that if he couldn't see it, it wouldn't bother him.

usage.en: Casual; often a self-soothing remark when avoiding something annoying.
usage.zh: 口语，多用于自我宽慰、回避烦心事。

pinyin: rén xīn gé dù pí
literal: person · heart · separated by · belly skin
natural: A person's heart is separated by a belly of skin

meaning.en: You can never really know what another person is thinking.
meaning.zh: 别人心里怎么想，你无法真正知道。

equivalents: You can never tell what's in another person's heart

examples.zh: 人心隔肚皮，做生意不能太轻信别人。
examples.en: You can never know what's in another's heart, so don't be too trusting in business.

examples.zh: 人心隔肚皮，他嘴上说支持，心里未必这么想。
examples.en: You can't see into people's hearts; he says he supports us, but he may not mean it.

usage.en: Usually a note of caution about trust; often followed by 知人知面不知心.
usage.zh: 多用于提醒对人要有戒心。

pinyin: qiáng lóng bù yā dì tóu shé
literal: strong · dragon · not · press down · local · snake
natural: Even a mighty dragon doesn't bully the local snake

meaning.en: An outsider, however powerful, should not push around the established locals on their home ground.
meaning.zh: 外来的强者也难以压服当地有势力的人。

equivalents: When in Rome, do as the Romans do
Don't mess with the locals

examples.zh: 到了人家的地盘，强龙不压地头蛇，说话办事都要客气点。
examples.en: On someone else's turf, even a dragon shouldn't bully the local snake, so be polite.

examples.zh: 这家连锁店刚进城，强龙不压地头蛇，生意并不好做。
examples.en: The chain just arrived in town and, with the local players entrenched, business isn't easy.

usage.en: Advises humility when operating in unfamiliar territory. Often used in business and travel.
usage.zh: 劝人到外地要谦让，多用于生意、出行等场合。

pinyin: chē dào shān qián bì yǒu lù
variants: 车到山前必有路，船到桥头自然直
literal: cart · reach · mountain · front · must · have · road
natural: When the cart reaches the mountain, there will be a road

meaning.en: Don't worry in advance; a way forward will appear when you get there.
meaning.zh: 事到临头总会有办法，不必提前发愁。

equivalents: We'll cross that bridge when we come to it
Something will turn up

examples.zh: 别太担心了，车到山前必有路。
examples.en: Don't worry too much; something will turn up.

examples.zh: 钱的事先不愁，车到山前必有路。
examples.en: Let's not fret about money yet; we'll find a way when the time comes.

usage.en: Optimistic reassurance; often paired with 船到桥头自然直. Can sound complacent if used to avoid planning.
usage.zh: 乐观的宽慰语，常与“船到桥头自然直”连用。

pinyin: chuán dào qiáo tóu zì rán zhí
literal: boat · reach · bridge · head · naturally · straight
natural: The boat will straighten out by the time it reaches the bridge

meaning.en: Problems tend to sort themselves out when the time comes, so don't worry beforehand.
meaning.zh: 事情到了眼前自然会有解决办法。

equivalents: It'll all work out in the end
We'll cross that bridge when we come to it

examples.zh: 先别急，船到桥头自然直。
examples.en: Don't panic yet; it will all sort itself out.

examples.zh: 房子的事，船到桥头自然直，到时候总有办法。
examples.en: About the house, it'll work out when the time comes.

usage.en: Reassuring, casual; the two halves 车到山前必有路 and this are often said together.
usage.zh: 口语宽慰语，常与“车到山前必有路”连用。

pinyin: sǐ mǎ dàng zuò huó mǎ yī
literal: dead · horse · treat as · live · horse · treat
natural: Treat a dead horse as if it were alive

meaning.en: Try every possible remedy even when the case looks hopeless.
meaning.zh: 明知希望渺茫，也要尽力试一试。

equivalents: Nothing to lose by trying
Clutch at straws

examples.zh: 反正没别的办法，就死马当作活马医吧。
examples.en: There's no other way anyway, so let's give it a try.

examples.zh: 这台电脑坏了，我死马当作活马医，拆开重装了一遍。
examples.en: The computer was dead, but I took it apart and reinstalled everything on the off chance.

usage.en: Often said when trying a long-shot solution. Casual, sometimes humorous.
usage.zh: 多用于最后一试，口语，略带自嘲。

pinyin: qiáng dǎo zhòng rén tuī
literal: wall · fall · crowd · people · push
natural: When the wall falls, everyone gives it a push

meaning.en: When someone falls from power or fortune, everybody piles on.
meaning.zh: 一个人倒了霉，大家都来落井下石。

equivalents: Kick a man when he's down
When the wall is falling, everyone shoves it

examples.zh: 他一出事，以前的朋友都来踩一脚，真是墙倒众人推。
examples.en: When he got into trouble, his old friends all piled on; it's a case of kicking a man when he's down.

examples.zh: 股价一跌，媒体也跟着批评，墙倒众人推。
examples.en: Once the share price dropped, the media piled in too.

usage.en: Usually a complaint about opportunism; often follows 破鼓万人捶.
usage.zh: 多用于感叹世态炎凉，常与“破鼓万人捶”连用。

pinyin: qíng rén yǎn lǐ chū xī shī
literal: lover · eyes · inside · produce · Xi Shi
natural: In a lover's eyes there appears a Xi Shi

meaning.en: To someone in love, the beloved looks beautiful, however ordinary.
meaning.zh: 对于有感情的人来说，对方在自己眼里最美。

equivalents: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder
Love is blind

examples.zh: 他女朋友长相普通，不过情人眼里出西施。
examples.en: His girlfriend is quite ordinary-looking, but beauty is in the eye of the beholder.

examples.zh: 情人眼里出西施，在妈妈眼里孩子永远最漂亮。
examples.en: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder; to a mother her child is always the loveliest.

usage.en: Xi Shi is the legendary beauty of ancient Yue. Often said teasingly about couples or parents.
usage.zh: 西施为春秋越国美女。常用来调侃恋人或父母。

pinyin: bú jiàn guān cái bù diào lèi
literal: not · see · coffin · not · shed · tears
natural: Doesn't cry until he sees the coffin

meaning.en: Refusing to give up or admit the truth until faced with undeniable disaster.
meaning.zh: 不到彻底失败、无可挽回的地步不肯死心认错。

equivalents: Won't believe it until it hits them in the face
None so blind as those who won't see

examples.zh: 劝了他多少次都不听，真是不见棺材不掉泪。
examples.en: We've warned him again and again, but he won't listen until disaster strikes.

examples.zh: 这种人不见棺材不掉泪，非得吃了大亏才肯认错。
examples.en: People like that won't admit fault until they've suffered a heavy loss.

usage.en: Criticism of stubbornness; 棺材 is read guān cai (cái). Often used with 不到黄河心不死.
usage.zh: 批评固执不悔，常与“不到黄河心不死”连用。

pinyin: bú dào huáng hé xīn bù sǐ
literal: not · reach · Yellow River · heart · not · die
natural: Won't give up until reaching the Yellow River

meaning.en: To refuse to give up until you have exhausted every possibility.
meaning.zh: 不达到目的或不到绝境决不罢休。

equivalents: Never say die
Won't take no for an answer

examples.zh: 他求了好几家公司，不到黄河心不死。
examples.en: He has applied to company after company; he just won't give up.

examples.zh: 你这是不到黄河心不死，撞了南墙才肯回头。
examples.en: You won't give up until you've hit a dead end.

usage.en: Can be neutral-positive (tenacity) or negative (stubbornness) depending on context.
usage.zh: 视语境可褒可贬，指执着或固执。

pinyin: rén xīn bù zú shé tūn xiàng
literal: human · heart · not · satisfied · snake · swallow · elephant
natural: The human heart is never satisfied, like a snake swallowing an elephant

meaning.en: People are insatiably greedy, always wanting more than they can handle.
meaning.zh: 人的贪心没有止境，总想得到更多。

equivalents: Give him an inch and he'll take a mile
Greed is bottomless

examples.zh: 他有了一套房还想要第二套，真是人心不足蛇吞象。
examples.en: He has one flat and wants a second; people are never satisfied.

examples.zh: 人心不足蛇吞象，贪心的人最后往往什么都得不到。
examples.en: Greedy people are never satisfied, and they usually end up with nothing.

usage.en: A warning against greed; often quoted in full or as 人心不足蛇吞象.
usage.zh: 告诫人不要贪心，常整句引用。

pinyin: tiān xià wū yā yì bān hēi
literal: under heaven · crow · all alike · black
natural: Crows everywhere are equally black

meaning.en: Bad people or corrupt officials are the same wherever you go.
meaning.zh: 到处的坏人坏事都一个样。

equivalents: They're all tarred with the same brush
One bad apple is like another

examples.zh: 天下乌鸦一般黑，换了哪个老板都一样。
examples.en: Crows are black everywhere; any boss would be the same.

examples.zh: 他说天下乌鸦一般黑，对官场彻底失望了。
examples.en: He said they are all as bad as each other and lost all hope in officialdom.

usage.en: Cynical, always derogatory. Often about officials, bosses or merchants.
usage.zh: 带愤世嫉俗色彩，含贬义，多指官场、老板等。

pinyin: lài há ma xiǎng chī tiān é ròu
literal: scabby · toad · want · eat · swan · meat
natural: A toad wants to eat swan meat

meaning.en: Someone of little standing hankering after something far beyond their reach, especially a romantic partner.
meaning.zh: 比喻不自量力，妄想得到条件远远高于自己的人或物。

equivalents: Aiming above one's station
A beggar on horseback

examples.zh: 他想追校花，别人都笑他是癞蛤蟆想吃天鹅肉。
examples.en: He wants to date the campus beauty, and everyone laughs that he's a toad dreaming of swan meat.

examples.zh: 你这想法是癞蛤蟆想吃天鹅肉，别做白日梦了。
examples.en: That idea is wishful thinking beyond your station; stop daydreaming.

usage.en: Derogatory and teasing; typically about someone's romantic pursuit. Can be used self-deprecatingly.
usage.zh: 含贬义，常用来讥笑别人追求不相称的对象，也可自嘲。

pinyin: qiān lǐ yīn yuán yí xiàn qiān
literal: thousand · li · marriage fate · one · thread · pull
natural: A thousand-li match is drawn by a single thread

meaning.en: Couples from far apart are brought together by fate.
meaning.zh: 相隔很远的男女，因缘分而被一根红线牵在一起。

equivalents: Marriages are made in heaven
Fate brings lovers together

examples.zh: 他们一个在北京，一个在广州，真是千里姻缘一线牵。
examples.en: One in Beijing and one in Guangzhou; it's fate that brought them together.

examples.zh: 婚礼上，司仪说：千里姻缘一线牵，祝你们白头偕老。
examples.en: At the wedding the host said, 'Fate has brought you together; may you grow old together.'

usage.en: Used in wedding speeches and about destiny in love. Often continued 有缘千里来相会.
usage.zh: 常用于婚礼致辞或感叹缘分。

pinyin: zhī rén zhī miàn bù zhī xīn
literal: know · person · know · face · not · know · heart
natural: You know a person's face but not his heart

meaning.en: You may know how someone looks and acts, but never what is truly in their heart.
meaning.zh: 能了解一个人的外表，却难以了解他的内心。

equivalents: You can't judge a book by its cover
Appearances can be deceiving

examples.zh: 知人知面不知心，他看上去老实，谁知是个骗子。
examples.en: You can know a person's face but not their heart; he seemed honest but turned out to be a fraud.

examples.zh: 交朋友要谨慎，毕竟知人知面不知心。
examples.en: Be careful in choosing friends, since you never know what is truly in a person's heart.

usage.en: A caution about trusting people; often used after being let down.
usage.zh: 提醒人对人不可轻信，多在被欺骗后感叹。

pinyin: jīn zhāo yǒu jiǔ jīn zhāo zuì
literal: today · have · wine · today · get drunk
natural: If there is wine today, get drunk today

meaning.en: Enjoy today and let tomorrow take care of itself.
meaning.zh: 有酒今天就痛快地喝，不去管明天的事，比喻只顾眼前享乐。

equivalents: Eat, drink and be merry
Live for today

examples.zh: 他整天今朝有酒今朝醉，一分钱也不存。
examples.en: He lives for today and saves not a penny.

examples.zh: 年轻人不要抱着今朝有酒今朝醉的态度过日子。
examples.en: Young people shouldn't live with an eat-drink-and-be-merry attitude.

story.en: Tang poet Luo Yin wrote in 'Self-Consolation': 'Today there is wine, so today I drink; if sorrow comes tomorrow, I'll be sad tomorrow.'
story.zh: 唐代罗隐《自遣》：“得即高歌失即休，多愁多恨亦悠悠。今朝有酒今朝醉，明日愁来明日愁。”

usage.en: Often critical when describing a carefree or improvident lifestyle; the full line continues 明日愁来明日愁.
usage.zh: 多含批评，形容只顾眼前、不计将来；原诗下句为“明日愁来明日愁”。
